coaching.coaching: Plan how verification gap in acceptance criteria will be verified in-session — restate any deferred or unobservable success target as an observable proxy.
coaching.subject: verification gap in acceptance criteria

metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

evidence: verify command `grep -rn 'bak-retarget' src/ .github/` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit first step to AC3's proving protocol: run `rebar fsck 2>&1 | sort | uniq -c > /tmp/fsck_before.txt` (or equivalent) BEFORE applying the deletion commit, then re-run the same command after and assert `diff /tmp/fsck_before.txt /tmp/fsck_after.txt` is empty.
evidence: Plan body says 'before/after count-by-kind comparison' but encodes no step ordering
Taxonomy item (7): 'missing prerequisite-state ordering — a command assumes state a prior step must establish'
AC3 text: 'zero new diagnostics' — without a captured before-snapshot this cannot be asserted
findings.finding: AC3's proving protocol requires capturing the 'before' rebar fsck diagnostic multiset BEFORE the deletion commit lands, but neither the plan body nor the AC steps describe this prerequisite capture step. An executing agent that deletes the directory first and then runs fsck has no baseline to compare against, making the 'identical multiset before and after' claim unverifiable.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC3: 'rebar fsck reports the identical diagnostic multiset before and after deletion'
scenarios: Agent runs deletion commit first, then runs fsck, obtains only the 'after' count. The 'before' count is lost and the criterion cannot be falsified.
A regression introduced by the deletion (e.g. a missing object reference) would be invisible if only the post-deletion count is checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Prepend to AC3: 'Step 0 (before deletion): run `rebar fsck 2>&1 | sort | uniq -c | tee /tmp/fsck_before.txt`; Step 2 (after deletion): run the same command into `/tmp/fsck_after.txt`; assert `diff /tmp/fsck_before.txt /tmp/fsck_after.txt` produces no output.' This makes the sequencing prerequisite explicit and produces a concrete artifact.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Supply a concrete proving command for AC2, e.g. `git clone <tickets-repo> /tmp/verify-clone && du -sb /tmp/verify-clone | awk '{print $1}'` compared before and after, or simply assert `git ls-tree -r HEAD | grep bak-retarget | wc -l` equals 0 and cite the known file sizes (33,025,572 + 15,186 = 33,040,758 bytes) as the expected savings.
evidence: No proving command cited for AC2 anywhere in the plan
File sizes are stated in the body (33,025,572 + 15,186 bytes) but no measurement protocol is given
AC1 has 'git ls-tree -r HEAD'; AC4 has a grep; AC2 has nothing analogous
findings.finding: AC2 ('Working-tree size of a fresh checkout drops by >=33 MB') has no concrete proving command. The tier is listed as 'repo measurement' but no `du`, `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, or equivalent command is supplied, so the criterion cannot be mechanically verified by an executing agent.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC2: 'Working-tree size of a fresh checkout drops by >=33 MB. Tier: repo measurement.'
scenarios: An automated verifier treating AC2 as requiring a fresh clone + disk measurement cannot proceed without guessing the command.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the AC2 tier note with: 'Proving command: `git ls-tree -lr HEAD | grep bak-retarget` returns no output (verifies removal); expected size reclaim: 33,025,572 + 15,186 = 33,040,758 bytes (~33 MB). A fresh checkout of HEAD must not contain `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/`.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the contradiction between 'No dependencies' and the explicit before-0303-692c sequencing requirement: replace 'No dependencies' with 'Must land before epic 0303-692c' (or equivalent blocking dependency notation) so the metadata and body agree.
evidence: 'It must land **before** epic 0303-692c's reclaim: the strip removes the directory from history, and the reclaim's re-add commit restores only the live `.bridge_state` files, so the tree-identity assertion depends on this already being gone.' — Why section
findings.finding: 'Scope: XS. No dependencies.' contradicts the hard sequencing constraint stated in Why: 'It must land before epic 0303-692c's reclaim … the tree-identity assertion depends on this already being gone.' An implementer reading the metadata footer would conclude there are no ordering constraints, while the body imposes a strict before-0303-692c gate. These two claims point in opposite directions about whether sequencing matters.
findings.location: Summary footer ('Scope: XS. No dependencies.') vs. Why section ('It must land before epic 0303-692c's reclaim')
scenarios: An implementer or merge-queue sees 'No dependencies' and allows 0303-692c to land first; the tree-identity assertion in 0303-692c then fails because the backup directory was not yet removed from HEAD.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the scope/dependency line to: 'Scope: XS. Outgoing dependency: must merge before epic 0303-692c (reclaim). No incoming dependencies.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend AC4's verification grep to include `tests/` and `scripts/` (e.g. `grep -rn 'bak-retarget' src/ .github/ tests/ scripts/`) so it actually confirms the test-file cleanup succeeded and covers the scripts/ naming pattern; add `scripts/retarget_jira_project.py` to the Files section if any reference there needs updating.
evidence: Plan AC4: "`grep -rn 'bak-retarget' src/ .github/` returns no production consumer"
Plan Files section: "tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_store_copy_isolation.py" named as a cleanup target — proves bak-retarget references exist in tests/
tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_store_copy_isolation.py:47: `".bridge_state.bak-retarget",` — hard-coded exact name in _NON_TICKET_ENTRIES set, not reachable by AC4's grep scope
tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_store_copy_isolation.py:158: comment `# (.bridge_state.bak-retarget) cannot survive by not being named explicitly` — also excluded from AC4 grep

scripts/retarget_jira_project.py:29: `sibling ``.bridge_state.bak-<label>`` directory` and line 127: `backup = bs.with_name(f".bridge_state.bak-{args.backup_label}")` — neither `scripts/` nor this file appears in AC4's scope or the Files cleanup inventory
findings.finding: AC4's consumer-enumeration uses an explicitly scoped grep (`grep -rn 'bak-retarget' src/ .github/`) that excludes `tests/` and `scripts/`. The plan's own Files section names `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_store_copy_isolation.py` as requiring cleanup of a hard-coded exact-name entry (`_NON_TICKET_ENTRIES` set literal, line 47, and comment line 158), which means AC4's stated grep will not verify that cleanup succeeded. Additionally, `scripts/retarget_jira_project.py` lines 29 and 127 reference the `.bridge_state.bak-<label>` naming pattern and are not covered by AC4's scope or the Files/cleanup inventory.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC4: "`grep -rn 'bak-retarget' src/ .github/` returns no production consumer. Tier: grep assertion."
scenarios: After the test cleanup commit, AC4's grep passes vacuously (tests/ excluded) even if the _NON_TICKET_ENTRIES entry at line 47 was not removed — giving a false green signal on a partially executed cleanup.

scripts/retarget_jira_project.py is not listed in the Files section and not covered by the AC4 grep; if it contains logic that references or regenerates .bridge_state.bak-retarget by name it would be silently unreviewed.
findings.suggested_fix: Change AC4 to: `grep -rn 'bak-retarget' src/ .github/ tests/ scripts/` returns no references (or only intentional pattern-generating uses in `scripts/retarget_jira_project.py` that do not hard-code the deleted directory name). Add `scripts/retarget_jira_project.py` to the Files section with a note that its `.bridge_state.bak-<label>` pattern reference needs no change (it generates the name dynamically) so reviewers know it was checked.
